meta.title: Install mtmux and open tmux in a browser in 2 minutes
meta.description: Install mtmux with npm, scan the code once, and reach your tmux sessions from any browser. Full CLI reference, self-hosting the broker and troubleshooting.

hero.title: Two minutes to your first mobile session.
hero.lead: No account, no config file, no reverse proxy. If tmux runs, mtmux attaches.

install.title: Install
install.requirements: Requires Node 22 or newer and <post>tmux installed</post>. Works on macOS, any glibc or musl Linux, and WSL2. The browser side needs nothing but WebSocket support, which every current browser has — there is no app to install and no account to create.

steps.label: Run it on the machine your tmux server is on
Scan the QR, or type the code at app.mtmux.com
steps.comment: the code is in the URL fragment, never sent to a server

steps.label: You're attached — check or stop the server any time
steps.comment: the browser is trusted from now on

note.label: note
note.body: Run <cmd>mtmux start --local</cmd> to skip the tunnel entirely: it serves loopback and your LAN and contacts no broker at all. <cmd>mtmux local</cmd> is the same thing, shorter.

cli.title: CLI reference
cli.pointer: Twenty-three commands, every flag, and the environment variables behind them — including share grants, device revocation and the token commands. It is generated from the CLI source, so it does not drift.

selfHosting.title: Self-hosting
selfHosting.pointer: mtmux is self-hosted by default: the CLI runs on your machine and holds its own token. Three degrees of independence beyond that — LAN-only, your own pairing broker, or the whole split deployment.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.pointer: Run mtmux doctor first — it checks Node, tmux, the port, config permissions and the broker. Twenty-five symptoms with causes and fixes, covering startup, connecting, pairing, the terminal, sessions, files and performance.

fullDocs: This page is the quickstart. The reference documentation — architecture, the sealed tunnel, the relay protocol, deployment and the web app — lives at <docsLink>docs.mtmux.com</docsLink>.
